title: Book Three · Chapter 86: The Bag from Grandmother's
story:
The last weeks of school pass. Spring becomes summer, and the holiday begins.

Leo's fifteenth reply arrives a week before the first Saturday. His aunt has bought the tickets. They will arrive at two in the afternoon and return three weeks later, on the fourth Saturday at ten in the morning.

He has read about Anna's visit. He says they can plan the books around that morning.

On the first Saturday, Ronan meets them outside the bus station. Leo notices the round shape in Ronan's bag.

“Your own ball?”

Ronan takes it out for him.

“Mine. Kai still has his.”

Leo turns the ball in his hands, then passes it back.

“Good birthday.”

“A very good birthday.”

The aunt smiles at both of them. She has three weeks of family things to do and no wish to stand outside the station all afternoon.

They take the local bus toward the old market. Ronan pays for his own seat. The aunt pays for herself and Leo. Their long journey and return tickets are already paid for too.

At the grandmother's, Ronan waits near the door while the family settles inside.

Leo comes back with a small cloth bundle.

“The books are here.”

“All yours?”

“Yes. Mum left them here before I went to my aunt's.”

He opens the bundle. There are a few more books than he wants to sell. Some have his name inside. One is a favourite story from his old school days.

He puts that one back.

Ronan looks at the cover.

“Too good to sell?”

“Not that. I still want it.”

Leo opens to a picture near the middle. He remembers the next part before he reads the words.

Ronan waits while he turns another page.

“We can leave it out,” he says.

Leo nods. He puts the favourite story behind his other things, away from the little bundle.

Ronan can see old school names on some covers. The books stayed here when Leo moved away. They do not all feel like things for a price card yet.

Leo chooses a second story and studies the name inside.

“This one can go.”

He puts it on the cloth. Then he looks through the other books more slowly.

Ronan does not choose for him. He holds the bundle open and lets Leo make the small pile himself. There will be enough books to look at tomorrow without taking the one Leo still wants to read.

“Three to start with,” he says. “We can choose tomorrow.”

The grandmother comes to the door. She knows about the idea. She points to the bundle.

“His books,” she says. “Not my cooking books.”

Leo grins. “Those would sell first.”

She shakes her head and takes her own book from the top of a nearby pile.

The aunt calls Leo to lunch. Ronan lifts his football bag and steps back.

“Tomorrow morning, at mine?” he asks.

“After nine. I need breakfast here first.”

“I know.”

Ronan walks home along the market road. At one stall, an old-book seller has several thin stories near the front.

He looks at the price cards. Then he asks the man about a small pile of ordinary books.

“Come back and choose,” the man says. “One yuan each from this pile.”

Ronan looks at the covers but buys nothing today.

At home, he puts his ball in the yard and takes his savings envelope down from the shelf. Tomorrow, he and Leo will count before they choose.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

bundle＝一包扎好的东西；favourite＝最喜欢的；settle＝安顿；yuan＝元。

## 理解问题

1. Leo这次什么时候到、什么时候回？家人和票款有没有安排？
2. 祖母家的哪些书能由Leo决定出售？Ronan在书摊有没有立即买一大堆？

## 读句子

**Ronan looks at the covers but buys nothing today.**

拆开看：Ronan / looks at the covers / but buys nothing today.

Ronan／看了看封面／但今天没有买书。
